newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Hyundai to invest $3.38 bln in Latin America.
newsitem.headline: Hyundai to invest $3.38 bln in Latin America.

text.p: South Korea's Hyundai Group said on Friday it plans to invest $3.38 billion in exploiting natural resources and participating in infrastructure projects in Brazil, Peru and Chile.

A Hyundai statement said the group planned to invest a total of $1.78 billion in Brazil, including the country's privatisation projects, in order to exploit iron ore, gold and cooper reserves. The group plans to buy a five percent stake of state-owned Compania Vale Do Rio Doce at about $500 million.
In a joint venture with the Mato Groso Do Sul state, Hyundai plans to invest $300 million to build power plants.

The statement said Hyundai would invest an estimated $700 million to build a car assembly plant to produce 100,000 units of passenger cars and commercial vehicles a year. The group said it would announce details of the plan soon.

The statement said the Hyundai group was also sure of winning a $255 million construction order to lay gas pipe lines which will link Bolivia and Brazil. It is the second stage of the 15-phase construction project valued at a total of $1.8 billion.
In Peru, Hyundai plans to invest a total of $1.3 billion to develop mines and build power plants.
In addition, the Hyundai group will spend $300 million to build a joint venture electrolytic copper refinery in Chile.
Hyundai said the group announced the plan to expand trade with the emerging Latin American market in line with a visit by South Korean President Kim Young-sam's visit.
Kim is to visit Latin America in September along with business leaders.
He will be the first South Korean president to visit the region, travelling to Brazil, Guatemala, Argentina and Peru.
The Hyundai statement said the group plans to sign letters of intent for some of the deals during the visit.
